_source: Computer-player rules not covered by the decoded tables: target values are heroes.exe's own (data/ai/tile_values.json, AITileValue) and buying is AIBuyer's (data/ai/buy_choice.json). This file keeps the day-1 treasury, the townless rule, the castle rebalance and the battle estimate.

starting_resources._comment: What every computer player owns on day 1, read from DOS saves of two independent new games (the Claw base save behind the ARENA*.GM1 files and GAME1.GM1 on another map), player block offset 125 (homm1-native-data.md 4.6). Both were made at the default opponent level; other levels are untested. The human in the same saves holds the Normal tuple from basic-concepts.md.

battle_estimate._source: heroes.exe 0x6e950, the computer's battle estimate (data/knowledge_base/research/ai-planner-decodes.md, 'Battle estimate'); constants from the data object at 0xa46..0xab2.
battle_estimate._comment: Against a neutral stack: Am = attacker rating x (neutral_base + neutral_per_level x AI level), Dm = defender rating, both at least 1. P = Am^e / (Am^e + Dm^e), e = exponent (exponent_large when either exceeds large). The first pessimism row whose 'below' exceeds P sets or shifts it. Expected own loss = trunc(A0 (1 - P) + trunc((1 - P) A0) P); the battle value is -loss x (loss_base - b1)^2 x f9. Ratings are plain count x rating: the original's count brackets and hero skill terms (0x73d34) are not ported. A computer route may pass one neutral stack (0x86b64 planning mode) and pays this cost for what lies beyond.

quick_battle._comment: Every fight a computer hero has with neutrals, a computer hero or a town no human holds is settled here, with no battle screen. P = the battle estimate's win chance; r = random(0..100) x draw_scale; the attacker wins when r < P. w = P for an attacker win, 1 - P otherwise; m = |r - P|, x (P + strong_bonus) when the attacker wins with P above strong_above. The winner loses loss = (m - 1)^2, squared again when w > sure_above and loss > sure_loss_above, at most (1 - w) x cap_share when w > cap_above. The loser loses everything, but a winning defender's own loss is loss x m. Each creature then dies when random(0..100) < trunc(fraction x 100), the first occupied stack keeps one unless fraction >= keep_one_below, and a side whose fraction reaches dead_at loses its hero.

townless._comment: bugs.md 25.2 item 1 (handbookhmm.ru/1-bugs), the Russian 1.1 behaviour; this heroes.exe is not English 1.0 (homm1-native-data.md 4.6). A computer player with no castle attacks the nearest castle whatever its army's strength, unless a noticeably weaker castle lies no more than two days away, and collects ownerless resources along the way. Ours: the weakest castle within castle_reach_days wins, the nearest breaks ties and is the target when none is that close; 'along the way' is a resource pile within detour_tiles steps; a day is 15 tiles, the scale AIController's distance discount already uses.

castle_swap._source: heroes.exe 0x746d8 (file offset), the computer's own-castle routine, read 2026-10-03; constants from the data object (file 0x1046a4 + 0xdda..0xe2a). The town-arrival handler 0x759c4 calls it once the castle is the hero's player's, so a capture runs it too. Checked against a DOS day-1/day-2 save pair (homm1-native-data.md 4.6): it reproduces all three heroes exactly.
castle_swap._comment: Strength is count x the native rating (data/creatures/join_power.json). The garrison's share of hero + garrison strength is steered toward base - per_skill * min(attack + defense, skill_cap): castle_* in a town with a castle, town_* otherwise. Nothing moves while the share is within tolerance x target. When the garrison holds too much, the hero takes and take_bonus is added to the gap. The strength to move is trunc(total x gap). Stacks go one at a time: first a stack whose creature is already on the other side, else the slowest (when leaving) or fastest (when taking), the stronger on a tie. A stack moves n = trunc(left / rating + round_bias) creatures, all of it when n reaches whole_stack_share of the stack (or all but one) and the remnant would be worth less than remnant_factor x (source strength - left). A leaving hero always keeps one creature. The loop stops after a stack worth more than left / overshoot.
